analysis.title: Intelligence weekly #132: September megacap tech results preview (Transformational Innovation Opportunities (TRIO): Artificial Intelligence)
key_insights: Heading into September-quarter megacap tech earnings, UBS CIO expects investors to focus on three themes: health of core businesses, the path to AI monetization, and the implications of the AI investment cycle for capex, margins and free cash flow.

Elevated capex is pressuring margins and free cash flow and may lead to capital raises in 2027. Management commentary on pricing, capacity constraints and AI returns will shape 2027 and later expectations.

After the sector's strong year-to-date rally expectations are elevated, and UBS sees potential for stock-specific pullbacks or profit-taking. It still expects a strong 3Q earnings season on fundamentals.

Positive tech guidance for the quarter (above sell-side expectations) is tracking at its highest level in 20 years. A record number of S&P 500 IT companies have guided above expectations (FactSet). The Nasdaq Composite is on track for more than 50% y/y 3Q earnings growth, driven by semiconductors and hardware.
UBS continues to favor platform and application beneficiaries of AI use cases. Within the enabling layer it likes infrastructure firms with strong pricing power and competitive positioning.

META (21 Oct): 2Q26 ad revenue grew 27% (14% impressions, 12% ad units). Consensus expects 23% y/y in 3Q with slight deceleration in 4Q. FY26 capex guidance is USD 130bn-145bn, and consensus free cash flow is deeply negative. Investors may be wary of any capex increase. Watch for comments on third-party capital structures (BlackRock agreement) and possible debt issuance.

META: The Meta Muse agentic consumer app has launched to strongly positive reviews and has bought some goodwill. UBS expects only a broad monetization framework without detail, and doubts much will be said on monetizing Muse Wonder. This is a near-term risk for investors expecting e-commerce estimate revisions.

MSFT (28 Oct): Azure grew 44% in the June quarter (42% in March 2026, 40% in June 2025). Management guided to about 45% for September. Published consensus matches guidance, but UBS suspects investor expectations are modestly higher. Spot GPU price increases are likely to be cited as a positive industry indicator, though the impact on Microsoft is limited by existing contracts.

MSFT: M365 Copilot grew about 50% last quarter to more than 30mn paid seats, roughly 6% penetration of the commercial base. Investors likely expect another 10mn seat adds. Microsoft is pivoting to a seat-plus-consumption pricing model, which should support growth over time but not as a step-function.

MSFT: Consensus expects just over USD 52bn of September-quarter capex (including leases) and a 51% y/y rise in FY27 (June) spending to USD 240bn. UBS sees moderate upward pressure on FY27 estimates. Azure gross margin is estimated to have compressed from about 60% in FY24 to the low 50% range. Microsoft's Maia 300 in-house chip is in inference production.

GOOG (28 Oct): Search is just over 60% of net revenue ex-TAC. It grew 17% y/y in June and is expected to slow to 15% in September and 13% in December on tougher comparisons. Investors want evidence that AI Overviews and AI Mode lift query volumes, and will ask about agentic AI competition.

GOOG: Google Cloud revenue rose 82% y/y to USD 24.8bn last quarter, well above consensus, partly from TPU chip sales, though core cloud also accelerated. Consensus is 92% (September) and 93% (December). UBS sees modest upside from AI compute demand, chip rental pricing and TPU sales. Sentiment on the Gemini roadmap improved after the late-September Gemini 4 Argon launch.
GOOG: Free cash flow turned negative for the first time in company history in the June quarter. Investors will watch FY27 spending, FCF and the potential for capital raises.

AMZN (30 Oct): AWS grew 37% y/y in June, its fastest in 18 quarters, with a backlog of USD 496bn (nearly double 4Q25). Consensus is 36% for both September and December. AWS margin reached a record 39.4%, but durability is debated (custom silicon, fixed-cost leverage and Bedrock versus higher memory costs and equipment spending).

AMZN: 2026 capex is guided to about USD 220bn (+66% y/y), mostly for AI and AWS. Consensus is 30% growth in 2027. Higher depreciation adds margin pressure, and investors will watch for further increases and capital raises.

AMZN: Advertising revenue grew 26% y/y in June (22% in 1Q), helped by Prime Day timing. Consensus expects deceleration to 17%. Consumer agentic apps such as Muse may reduce page views and threaten ad revenue.

AAPL (2 Nov): Management guided September-quarter revenue growth of 9-11% y/y (16% in June), reflecting constrained advanced-node chip supply. iPhone 18 launched Pro and Pro Max before base models. Supply-chain reports are mixed, with some order cuts for 18 Pro components.

AAPL: Consensus gross margin is 47.6% for September versus 48.0% prior. DRAM and NAND are tight and elevated, with memory costs a more than 120bps hit in June. Apple raised prices across its iPhone line. Tariff refunds boosted June gross margin by 250bps and are guided to add 100bps in September. Price increases may not fully offset memory costs.

AAPL: Apple Intelligence is off to a slow start. Third-party agentic apps could disintermediate Apple from search, App Store advertising and take rates, though UBS sees Siri AI as a possible agentic layer. UBS does not expect much tangible progress.

Chinese hyperscalers (reporting from mid-November): Sentiment has deteriorated, valuations are near multi-year lows below 12x forward P/E, and positioning is subdued. High-teens earnings growth next year and an emerging positive revision trend lead UBS to see risk skewed to the upside, though no obvious near-term catalyst exists.

Alibaba (mid-November): After multiple quarters of EBITA downgrades since June 2025, UBS expects an earnings inflection: stabilizing core e-commerce EBITA, accelerating cloud revenue with better margins, and narrowing new-business losses. UBS raised next-year earnings estimates and expects Alibaba to outperform the sector. A recent equity placement is a near-term overhang, but another raise within six months is seen as unlikely.

Tencent (18 Nov): UBS expects it to stay range-bound near term, with negative revisions likely lasting longer than Alibaba's because its AI investment phase started late. It sees limited downside, and potential re-rating if the AI trade broadens from infrastructure to agents and applications.

market_movers.rationale: UBS expects an earnings inflection and the start of a positive revision cycle, and expects Alibaba to outperform the sector.
Muse launch has bought goodwill, but capex and free cash flow are the debate going into 21 October earnings.
Azure guided to about 45%, with investor expectations modestly above consensus.
AWS growth is at an 18-quarter high with a USD 496bn backlog, with margin durability debated.
Cloud grew 82% y/y and UBS sees modest upside to consensus, but free cash flow turned negative.
Supply constraints and memory costs weigh on growth and gross margin.

sector_views.rationale: Record positive guidance and more than 50% Nasdaq 3Q EPS growth, though expectations are elevated and pullbacks are possible.
Valuations below 12x forward P/E, low expectations, high-teens earnings growth next year and an emerging positive revision trend.

earnings_insights: META reports 21 October. 2Q26 ad revenue growth was 27% (reported). Consensus estimate for 3Q ad revenue growth is 23% y/y. FY26 capex guidance is USD 130bn-145bn.

MSFT reports 28 October. Azure growth was 44% in the June quarter (reported). Management guided about 45% for September, in line with published consensus. Consensus capex estimate is just over USD 52bn for the September quarter and USD 240bn for FY27 (+51%).

GOOG reports 28 October. Search grew 17% y/y in June (reported). Consensus estimate is 15% for September and 13% for December. Google Cloud revenue was USD 24.8bn, +82% y/y in June (reported). Consensus estimate for cloud growth is 92% (September) and 93% (December).

AMZN reports 30 October. AWS grew 37% y/y in June (reported) with a USD 496bn backlog. Consensus estimate is 36% for September and December. Advertising grew 26% in June (reported). Consensus estimate for 3Q ad growth is 17%. 2026 capex guidance is about USD 220bn.
AAPL reports 2 November. Management guided September-quarter revenue growth of 9-11% y/y (16% in June, reported). Consensus estimate for gross margin is 47.6% versus 48.0% in the prior quarter.

Alibaba reports mid-November and Tencent on 18 November. UBS expects Alibaba core e-commerce EBITA to stabilize and cloud growth to accelerate. Chinese hyperscalers are expected to report 3Q26 from mid-November.
Nasdaq Composite 3Q EPS growth is tracking above 50% y/y (UBS and FactSet estimate), driven by semiconductors and hardware.

trade_ideas.description: Favor Alibaba (BABA) into mid-November earnings as the Chinese hyperscaler with positive earnings revisions
trade_ideas.rationale: Earnings inflection expected, with cloud acceleration and narrowing new-business losses, and UBS expects outperformance versus the sector.
trade_ideas.risk: Recent equity placement could remain a near-term overhang. Macro headwinds in China and intensified competition.

trade_ideas.description: Tencent (700 HK) re-rating if the AI trade broadens from infrastructure to agents and applications
trade_ideas.rationale: Tencent would be a more natural beneficiary of a rotation, even before earnings revisions turn.
trade_ideas.risk: Negative revision cycle may last longer and constrain upside.

risk_factors: Elevated expectations after the tech rally, with potential for pullbacks and profit-taking.
Higher capex pressuring margins and free cash flow, with possible capital raises in 2027.
Run-rate growth questions at leading AI labs, and an uncertain macro backdrop.
Agentic AI apps such as Meta Muse disintermediating Apple, Amazon advertising and Google Search.
Memory cost pressure on Apple gross margin and supply constraints on iPhone 18.
China macro weakness, uncertain AI investment returns and higher global yields for Chinese hyperscalers.
vol_and_positioning: Chinese hyperscaler investor positioning is described as subdued with no investor interest, and valuations are at a strong support level.
The report expects asymmetric outcomes for Chinese hyperscalers into 3Q earnings: limited downside on misses, potentially meaningful upside on positive surprises.
Elevated expectations after the tech rally raise the potential for stock-specific pullbacks or profit-taking.
geopolitical: US-China tensions are listed in the risk table for Applied Materials, ASM Pacific and others.
The Chinese government continues to support domestic semiconductor capabilities, per the Infineon and STMicroelectronics risk statements.
The Meta ad outlook is subject to geopolitical tensions in some regions, per the report.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong demand, record positive guidance, cloud acceleration (Azure 44%, AWS 37%, Google Cloud 82%) and a Nasdaq 3Q EPS growth above 50%.
tension_points.bear_case: Elevated capex is pressuring free cash flow (Google FCF negative, Meta consensus FCF deeply negative) and may require capital raises in 2027, with expectations elevated after the rally.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Management raising capex guidance without matching revenue acceleration, or announcing capital raises or debt issuance to fund the gap.

tension_points.bull_case: Valuations below 12x forward P/E, high-teens earnings growth next year and an emerging positive revision trend.
tension_points.bear_case: Weak China macro, aggressive AI investment with uncertain returns and pressure on multiples from higher global yields.
